Section 232 derivative-product duty extended to agricultural machinery under HS 8432 and 8433 (designated HS6 lines) by Proclamation 11021, effective 2026-04-06. This is an IMPORT duty into the US - it raises Deere's cost on machines and components imported from Europe/Mexico/India/Japan

Rate cut from 25% to 15% effective 2026-06-08 by the 1 June 2026 proclamation, running through 2027-12-31. Falls INSIDE Deere FY2026 Q3 (4 May - 2 Aug 2026), so roughly the last 8 weeks of Q3 carried the lower rate

Section 122 of the Trade Act of 1974: additional 10pp ad valorem on all imports regardless of origin, imposed 2026-02-24 to replace the struck-down IEEPA tariffs. Goods already subject to Section 232 were excepted

US Court of International Trade held Proclamation 11012 ultra vires and entered permanent injunctive relief, striking the 10% Section 122 baseline on 2026-05-07 - three days into Deere FY2026 Q3. Zero here is a real measured rate (duty struck down), not a missing value
Supreme Court decision 2026-02-20 invalidating tariffs imposed under IEEPA (6-3). Confirmed in Deere's own Q2 FY2026 10-Q, so this is a company-corroborated fact, not just press reporting

CBP declaration filed with the CIT on 2026-08-04 reporting status as at 2026-07-31: >75,000 CAPE declarations submitted and 17.69m validated entries liquidated without IEEPA tariffs; ~$128.68bn of potential and certified refunds accepted for processing. Economy-wide figure, NOT Deere-specific
CBP activated phase one of the IEEPA refund process (CAPE - Consolidated Administration and Processing of Entries) on 2026-04-20. Deere's $272m Q2 claim was filed under this phase

CAPE phase 2 opened 2026-06-29, covering reconciliation entries, AD/CVD entries and finally-liquidated entries. Inside Deere FY2026 Q3 - the mechanism through which any additional Q3 recovery would be claimed
CAPE phase 3 reported on track for end of July 2026. Note the government has appealed the CIT refund order to the Federal Circuit, so refunds carry reversal risk

Deere Q3 FY2025 10-Q: "On August 18, 2025, the scope of steel and aluminum derivative duties was expanded to include additional Harmonized Tariff Schedule codes." Section 232 metals duties were NOT affected by the IEEPA ruling and persist through FY2026
